name: UX DataTables Documentation
description: The documentation site for a Symfony bundle that renders DataTables.net grids from a PHP class.

roles.accent: indigo — every interactive commitment; the only saturated color at rest
roles.focus: amber — the focus halo only, never a surface, border, or text color
roles.citation: crimson — used where Symfony itself is meant, and for danger asides
roles.neutral: slate — page field, surfaces, rules, and the three-step text ramp

shadows.usage: Shadow is reserved for elements out of the document flow: 1 = the demonstrative sample table, 2 = the mobile drawer, 3 = the search dialog. Structure is drawn with 1px rules.

motion.signature: row-settle: after a sort, sample-table rows re-enter with a 45ms-per-row stagger. Every animation is gated behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
motion.focusRing: 2px solid var(--focus) at 2px offset, over an amber halo: color-mix(in srgb, var(--amber-500) 55%, transparent)

breakpoints.600: The sample table drops its least important column.
breakpoints.1000: The sidebar becomes a <dialog> drawer, opened from a sticky bar showing Section / Page.
breakpoints.1180: The table of contents collapses into a <details> panel under the header.

narrative.northStar: The Well-Composed Table — the site borrows the vocabulary of the thing it documents: a strict grid, a frozen header, an active row, a sort direction, so the reader is already inside a DataTable while reading about one.

namedRules.The One Accent Rule: Indigo is the only saturated color on a page at rest. Amber may not paint a surface, a border, or text — it exists as the focus halo. Crimson appears only where Symfony is the subject.
namedRules.The Two-Theme Rule: Dark is declared twice: once as @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) :root:not([data-theme='light']) for visitors before the theme script runs or with JavaScript off, once as :root[data-theme='dark'] so the toggle wins in both directions. A color defined in only one of the two is a bug.
namedRules.The Primitive Containment Rule: Ramps are referenced only inside tokens.css. Every other file reads semantic tokens, so a theme change is a one-file change.
namedRules.The Single H1 Rule: The h1 and the one-line summary come from frontmatter and are rendered once by the layout. No page body writes its own title; the build test asserts exactly one h1 per page.
namedRules.The Column-Header Rule: Uppercase, wide-tracked micro-type is how the site says 'this labels a group' — sidebar sections, aside kinds, table headers. It is never used for a sentence.
namedRules.The Rule-Over-Shadow Rule: Structure is drawn with 1px solid var(--rule). A shadow is only allowed on something that has actually left the flow — dialog, drawer, or the one demonstrative table.

dos: Draw structure with 1px solid var(--rule) and tone changes, the way the site's own three-column shell is drawn.
Read semantic tokens (--accent, --text-muted, --rule) in every file except tokens.css.
Declare a new themed color in all three places: light :root, the prefers-color-scheme: dark block, and :root[data-theme='dark'].
Ship behavior that degrades: content, navigation, theme, and tables must work with JavaScript disabled, and enhancement controls are injected by script rather than authored dead in the markup.
Keep the accent for interaction and position; a decorative use of indigo weakens every functional one.
donts: Add a shadow to something that has not left the document flow.
Use a grid of same-size icon-and-heading cards as page structure; sections are entered through lists of their real pages.
Paint with amber. It is the focus halo and warning tone, nothing else.
Use crimson except where Symfony itself is the subject, or for a danger aside.
Hardcode the site's base path in a link; withBase() owns it, and authored MDX links stay root-relative.
Write an h1 in page content — the layout renders the frontmatter title once.
Introduce permanent zebra striping or a second accent hue to add 'variety' to a dense page; density is carried by rules and spacing.
